source.title: Data Scaling Laws for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
source.authors: Alexander Naumann; Xun-Jiang Gu; Tolga Dimlioglu; Mariusz Bojarski; Alperen Değirmenci; Alexander Popov; Devansh Bisla; Marco Pavone; Urs Muller; B. Ivanovic

record.tranche_reason: The study extends data-scaling analysis to end-to-end autonomous driving and reports scaling and extrapolation results using trajectory errors and closed-loop driving outcomes, rather than language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study varies driving-data size, fits estimators to trajectory metrics, and measures open- and closed-loop outcomes. The language-model studies cited in the related-work section are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study fits power-law estimators to the test error of driving models trained on 16h to 8192h of data, about 2.7 orders of magnitude. It then checks how those fits extrapolate to larger splits. This bears on V5: whether the power-law form holds in a non-text imitation-learning setting. The claim's V2 and V7 concern language-model pretraining laws, so their driving-domain analogues are recorded under V5 and fits_no_version rather than as direct tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim that surround-view inputs are 'essential' for complex maneuvers, although the measured gain was a modest 4-5% at 512h. They frame the estimator as fitting well but optimistic out of sample.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales driving-dataset hours for an imitation-learning trajectory-prediction model and evaluates FDE, ADE, MR, and simulated MDBF. It does not measure language-model cross-entropy or vary language-model parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Scaling trends vary by action type and metric; estimator choice and the number of training points change fit and extrapolation results; backbone size changes data requirements; camera count has a modest benefit for complex maneuvers at the reported 512h setting.

fits_no_version.finding: In driving imitation learning, open-loop error keeps improving with data, but closed-loop distance before failure plateaus around 1 km beyond 256h. Larger planner heads and augmentation do not lift this plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gains in non-text training loss under scaling do not carry over predictably to closed-loop or deployment performance (a V6 analogue outside LMs).

fits_no_version.finding: Power-law-with-offset fits on small driving-data runs systematically underestimate the data needed to reach targets 2x to 4x beyond the fitted range.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extrapolation of data scaling laws outside LM pretraining is optimistic (a V2 analogue in other domains).

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: The authors note optimistic out-of-sample data estimates and that collecting measurements averaged over multiple runs could reduce noise but would require more compute and time. Closed-loop evaluation covers two highway scenarios with minimal traffic interactions; real-world testing was not conducted.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported numeric outcome for the initial 1024h and 2048h validation MSE comparisons was extracted beyond the estimator comparisons and extrapolation results recorded above.

untested.parts: LM loss extrapolation; the driving extrapolation spans only 4x, not orders of magnitude.
Entirely: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Power laws in parameters or compute (only two backbone sizes); repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer.
LM exponents and compute-optimal split disagreements.

missing.what: Planner head capacity scaling (256/512/1024) with ResNet-18 did not alleviate the closed-loop plateau
Authors state the plateau appears only above about 10^3 hours, with near-linear log-log trends before that
Three-camera overall FDE comparable to one camera from 16h to 1024h

record.verdict_notes: This is a non-LM domain, so all rows bear on V5 at most. The driving-domain analogues of V2 (extrapolation) and V7 (fit dependence, bending) are folded into V5 limits_scope and fits_no_version rather than labelled as tests of the LM versions. The study has single runs with no seed averaging, and its epoch schedule decreases with data size, which may affect the fitted curve. The reader's V7 label citing r28 was not linked to that version.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss of language models as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
The study tests extrapolation for driving-model trajectory error, not language-model loss; it does not test runs orders of magnitude larger than the fitted runs.
No fixed-compute optimization of parameter and token allocation, or growth laws for an optimal split.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture at a fixed parameter count.
Tests data scaling for an autonomous-driving task, not image or video generation, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream language-model task performance or relationship between language-model pretraining loss and downstream performance.
The study examines estimator and fitting choices for driving-data scaling, but not language-model exponents or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.

rows.measure: Distance driven before departure from the drivable area

rows.note: The study says increasing open-loop performance did not produce proportional closed-loop benefits.

relationships.condition: Open-loop driving trajectory error (FDE, ADE, MR) vs data hours, ResNet-18, 16h to 8192h
relationships.reason: A power law with an irreducible offset fits all actions and metrics, with c around -0.35 to -0.42 (r1, r2, r4, r5, r6, r12).
relationships.display_finding: Offset power laws fitted trajectory errors with c around −0.35 to −0.42, while turning required a shifted form with c=0.110.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Open-loop driving trajectory error (FDE, ADE, MR) vs data hours, ResNet-18, 16h to 8192h
source_check.reason: The condition includes turning, which uses M3 with c = 0.110 and a shift term, rather than the claimed offset power law with c around -0.35 to -0.42. The full condition has mixed evidence; supports is appropriate after narrowing it to the M2 action and metric fits.

relationships.condition: Pure power law, turning, and extrapolation beyond the fitted range
relationships.reason: The pure power law fails (r11). Turning needs a shift term and plateaus (r3). Fits through 2048h underpredict the data needed at 4096h and 8192h (r15 to r18). Extrapolation quality is unstable across the number of fit points (r7 to r10).
relationships.display_finding: A pure power law failed, turning required a shift term and plateaued, and fits through 2048 hours underestimated data requirements at 4096 and 8192 hours, with extrapolation sensitive to the number of fitted points.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Pure power law, turning, and extrapolation beyond the fitted range
source_check.reason: M1 fails to capture the trend while M2 fits, and turning requires shifted M3, qualifying the functional form. Extrapolation errors are auxiliary evidence about estimator reliability, not independent failures of V5; lane changing overpredicts the 8192h requirement as 10,000h.

relation.reason: Its own experiments vary training-data hours and compare candidate scaling functions against open-loop driving errors.

tranche.reason: The study directly tests data-scaling forms in a new setting: end-to-end autonomous-driving imitation learning.

source_check.notes: Table 2 coefficients describe action-normalized FDE, with each action's maximum mapped to 1.0. Figure 10's caption says full dataset, but Sections 5.2 and Appendix D specify fitting through 512h and validation at 1024h/2048h.

statements.correction: M1 held-out MSE = 0.074; M2 held-out MSE = 0.006. Fitting sizes = 16–512h; validation sizes = 1024h and 2048h. Turning uses M3, y = β(x^-1 + γ)^c, with β = 1.365, c = 0.110, γ = 0.0004. Authors report consistent turning scaling through 8192h and an emerging plateau thereafter; maximum measured dataset = 8192h. V5 verdict for these qualifications = limits_scope.
statements.problem: The driving findings are accurately summarized, but a challenges classification overstates them: offset power laws fit other actions and metrics, while turning requires a shifted form. A plateau beyond the maximum measured dataset is not an independently observed result.
